baggage-dolly.context: A low open cart on four small wheels with a tow bar at one end and two suitcases on its flat deck. Used for airport ground handling, baggage logistics and luggage delivery.

underseat-bag.context: An airline seat in side view with a small soft bag tucked on the floor beneath it. Used for cabin baggage rules, personal item allowances and airline fee pages.

explosive-trace-swab.context: A paddle with a round swab pad held up beside a small carry-on bag with a top handle. Used for airport security screening, explosives trace checks and baggage inspection notices.

security-pat-down.context: A standing person with arms held out sideways while a smaller figure runs a hand down their side. Used for airport security checks, body searches and screening procedures.

ambulift.context: A truck with its passenger cabin raised on a scissor lift up to the level of an aircraft door. Used for assisted boarding of wheelchair users and passengers with reduced mobility.

cabin-reading-light.context: A ceiling panel with a round lamp casting beams of light downward onto a passenger seat. Used for in-flight comfort controls, seat settings and cabin lighting.

overhead-air-vent.context: A round swivel nozzle set in a ceiling panel with three wavy air lines flowing out of it. Used for cabin comfort, ventilation controls and in-flight air adjustment.

aircraft-lavatory.context: A narrow cubicle seen from the front with a compact toilet and a tiny sink on the wall. Used for airplane restroom signs, seat maps and cabin facility lists.

cabin-crew-jumpseat.context: A fold-down seat attached to a cabin wall, shown open with a shoulder harness across its back. Used for cabin crew seating, emergency exit rows and flight attendant procedures.

cockpit-door.context: A reinforced flight deck door with a peephole and handle, and a keypad beside it. Used for flight deck security, locked access areas and crew-only zones.

cockpit.context: A flight deck seen from behind with angled windshield panes above two seat backs. Used for pilot views, flight deck tours and cockpit features.

pilot-wings.context: A badge with a small central shield and a feathered wing swept out on each side. Used for pilot qualifications, aviation clubs, flight school and airline crew ranks.

pilot-flight-bag.context: A boxy hard-sided case with a carry handle on top and a front flap held by two latches. Used for pilot supplies, headsets, flight kit and crew luggage.

kneeboard.context: A small clipboard held to a thigh by elastic straps, with note lines on its face. Used for in-flight notes, checklists and quick reference cards.

electronic-flight-bag.context: A tablet screen showing a small airplane symbol, held in a clamp mount below it. Used for digital charts, flight planning and paperless cockpit tools.

aeronautical-chart.context: A folded map sheet with panel creases and an airport mark on its middle panel. Used for flight navigation, route planning and airspace maps.

e6b-flight-computer.context: A round slide rule with concentric rings and a small window in the middle. Used for manual flight calculations such as wind correction, fuel burn and time-speed-distance.

preflight-checklist.context: A card with a small airplane mark at the top and a column of ticked boxes. Used for pilot checks before takeoff, safety procedures and inspection forms.

sidestick.context: A short control stick with a rounded grip rising from a side console, with an armrest behind it. Used for fly-by-wire controls, flight simulators and cockpit hardware.

flap-lever.context: A slim slotted gate with a handle bar slid across it and notches beside it. Used for flap settings, throttle quadrant controls and cockpit procedures.

landing-gear-lever.context: A cockpit panel with a round wheel-shaped knob above a vertical slot. Used for raising and lowering landing gear, retraction states and cockpit controls.

trim-wheel.context: A tall ridged wheel set into a console beside a pointer scale. Used for pitch trim settings, cockpit controls and aircraft balance adjustments.

airspeed-indicator.context: A round gauge with a needle and a curved arc band around its edge. Used for speed readouts, flight instruments and dashboard dials.

vertical-speed-indicator.context: A round gauge with a needle resting at the left zero mark and tick marks above and below. Used for climb and descent rates in flight instruments and dashboards.

horizontal-situation-indicator.context: A round gauge with a small airplane mark in the center, a course arrow and a deviation bar. Used for navigation heading displays and instrument approach training.

turn-coordinator.context: A round gauge with a small banked airplane seen from behind and a ball in a curved tube below it. Used for turn and slip indications and basic flight instruments.

whiskey-compass.context: A small liquid compass housing on a stem, with a window showing a card with the letter N. Used for standby heading references and cockpit backup instruments.

primary-flight-display.context: A screen with a horizon line in the middle and a tape on each side for speed and altitude. Used for glass cockpit displays and flight instrument screens.

navigation-display.context: A screen with a curved compass arc, a short route line and a small airplane triangle at the bottom. Used for moving maps, route displays and glass cockpit navigation.

autopilot.context: A control strip with an airplane mark in the center and a round knob on each side. Used for autoflight modes, cockpit panels and hands-off flying settings.

ground-proximity-warning.context: A mountain peak beside a warning triangle with an exclamation mark. Used for terrain alerts, pull-up warnings and cockpit safety systems.

collision-avoidance-display.context: A round screen with a small airplane dot at the center, a dashed range ring and a diamond traffic mark ahead. Used for traffic alerts and airborne collision warning systems.

stall-warning.context: A steeply tilted wing cross section with airflow curling into a swirl above it and an exclamation mark. Used for aerodynamic stall alerts and flight training warnings.

master-caution.context: A square cockpit push button with glow lines around it and a bold bar across its face. Used for warning lights, caution annunciators and alert acknowledgements.

flight-management-computer.context: A cockpit keypad unit with a small screen on top, side keys and a grid of keys below. Used for entering flight plans, routes and performance data.

pitot-tube.context: A straight probe pointing forward from a curved fuselage skin with a small opening at its tip. Used for airspeed sensing, air data systems and aircraft sensor diagrams.

angle-of-attack-vane.context: A small wedge-shaped weather vane on a round base. Used for angle-of-attack sensing, air data sensors and aircraft maintenance diagrams.

winglet.context: A wing seen from the front with its tip turning sharply upward into a tall swept fin. Used for aircraft design, fuel saving features and airliner parts lists.

aileron.context: A swept wing seen from above with the outer rear panel shaded and a curved line showing it hinge. Used for roll control, flight control surface diagrams and flight training.

wing-flap.context: A wing cross section with a smaller curved panel lowered down and back from its trailing edge. Used for high lift devices, takeoff and landing configurations and aerodynamics teaching.

thrust-reverser.context: A jet engine pod with its rear cowl slid back and curved arrows pointing forward. Used for landing braking systems and engine maintenance diagrams.

auxiliary-power-unit.context: A tapered tail cone with a small exhaust slot near its tip and heat lines streaming out. Used for onboard power, ground operations and aircraft systems diagrams.

cargo-door.context: A fuselage side with a large rectangular hatch hinged open upward above the cargo compartment. Used for freight loading, belly cargo and ground handling procedures.

aircraft-door.context: A tall plug door with rounded top corners, a small round window and a lift handle. Used for cabin doors, boarding points and emergency exit diagrams.

cargo-hold.context: A round fuselage cross section with seats on the upper deck and two cargo containers below the floor. Used for belly freight, passenger and cargo layouts and loading diagrams.

airplane-wing.context: A swept wing seen from above with an engine pod ahead of its front edge. Used for aircraft structure, wing lists and airliner parts diagrams.

glide-slope.context: An airplane descending along a dashed line down to a runway line. Used for approach paths, landing guidance and instrument landing explanations.

instrument-landing-system.context: Three antenna masts standing along the end of a runway with radio waves arcing from the middle one. Used for precision approach guidance and runway navigation aids.

vor-beacon.context: A cone-shaped ground station topped with a short spike and ringed by small antennas. Used for radio navigation, air routes and navigation aid maps.

non-directional-beacon.context: A tall radio mast held by guy wires with radio waves arcing out from its top. Used for ADF navigation, radio beacon maps and signal towers.

papi-lights.context: A row of four square light units, two solid and two outlined, above a ground line. Used for runway approach guidance showing a correct glide path by color.

runway-edge-lights.context: A runway seen in perspective with rows of light dots down both sides, growing larger toward the viewer. Used for night operations and airfield lighting.

runway-centerline-lights.context: A runway in perspective with two edge lines and a single line of lights growing larger down its center. Used for low visibility operations and airfield lighting.

touchdown-zone-markings.context: A runway from above with two edge lines and pairs of short parallel bars on both sides of the center. Used for runway paint markings and landing zones.

aiming-point-markings.context: A runway from above with two long thick blocks either side of a dashed centerline. Used for runway markings that show the landing target point.

runway-holding-position-sign.context: An airport ground sign on short legs showing a pair of runway numbers split by a dash. Used for hold-short points, taxiway signage and airfield rules.

runway-distance-remaining-sign.context: A square airport sign on short legs showing one large digit. Used for showing thousands of feet of runway left and airfield signage.

stop-bar-lights.context: A taxiway entrance from above with edge lines and a straight row of lights across it. Used for runway incursion protection and taxiway hold lines.

runway-guard-lights.context: A pair of round lamps on a short post with flash rays beside one lamp. Used for flashing hold-short warnings at runway entrances.

wind-tee.context: An airplane-shaped wind indicator seen from above with a cross-shaped body. Used for airfield wind direction and landing direction signals.

landing-tetrahedron.context: A pyramid-shaped wind indicator with a pointed nose, held above a pivot post and base. Used for airfield wind direction and landing direction markers.

signal-square.context: A square ground panel with a bar and two end bars painted in the middle. Used for airfield ground signals and airstrip visual markers.

light-gun.context: A handheld signal lamp with a flared head, a pistol grip and three straight light beams. Used for tower signals to aircraft with radio failure and lamp signaling.

airport-beacon.context: A short tower with a round lamp on top casting two opposite beams. Used for locating airfields at night and aviation light signals.

runway-visual-range.context: Two sensor heads on posts facing each other across a gap with short fog lines between them. Used for measuring visibility along a runway in fog and low cloud.

arresting-gear.context: A jet seen from above hooking a cable stretched across the runway so the cable pulls into a V. Used for emergency stops and carrier or military runway landings.

arrestor-bed.context: An aircraft nose wheel on a strut sinking into a block bed with textured dots at the end of a runway. Used for overrun protection and runway safety areas.

blast-fence.context: A curved slatted wall with exhaust lines blowing toward it from the left. Used for jet blast protection, engine run-up areas and apron safety.

bird-scarer.context: A gas cannon with a flared barrel propped on a tripod, with a small bird flying away. Used for wildlife control and bird strike prevention at airfields.

foreign-object-debris.context: A broken tire tread piece lying on pavement with a loose bolt and small fragments beside it. Used for runway sweeps and objects that can damage aircraft.

follow-me-car.context: A small car in side view with a checkered sign on its roof. Used for airport vehicles that guide aircraft to parking positions.

aircraft-tow-bar.context: A long bar on two small wheels with a ring towing eye at one end and a forked head at the other. Used for pushback, towing planes and ground handling equipment.

ground-power-unit.context: A boxy wheeled cart with a coiled reel on its side and a thick cable ending in a large plug. Used for powering parked aircraft and ground support equipment.

preconditioned-air-unit.context: A box unit with a corrugated hose curving up toward the underside of a fuselage. Used for cooling or heating a parked aircraft without running its engines.

lavatory-service-truck.context: A small service truck with a round tank on its back and a hose reaching up toward a fuselage. Used for emptying and refilling aircraft toilets on the ground.

fuel-hydrant-pit.context: An open pit in the apron pavement with a lid raised and a hose connected to the valve inside. Used for refueling aircraft from underground fuel lines.

wing-walker.context: A ground crew figure in a vest holding a raised baton beside a wing tip. Used for marshalling, wing clearance checks and apron safety.

aircraft-maintenance-dock.context: An airplane tail rising in the middle of a scaffold with posts, a platform and railings. Used for hangar maintenance, repair bays and access stands.

aircraft-jack.context: A tripod jack with a vertical ram lifting the underside of a wing. Used for raising aircraft for wheel changes, weighing and maintenance.
